step1_analysis.description: This is a lumped-element equivalent circuit model of a coupled standing-wave oscillator's resonant tank. It models the transmission line segments as an inductive T-network (LA_1, LA_2, LB_2) with tank capacitances (C_1, C_2) and losses (RL_1, RL_2), while current sources represent the active device injection.

paper_reference.title: A 10-GHz Global Clock Distribution Using Coupled Standing-Wave Oscillators

resonant_frequency.description: The frequency at which the tank impedance is maximized, corresponding to the natural oscillation frequency.

sky130_expected.calculation: Determined by passive L and C values. f_res = 1 / (2*pi*sqrt(L_eq*C_eq)). With L_eq=300pH and C_eq=0.84pF (even mode), f_res is exactly 10 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The resonant frequency is set by the passive components to match the paper's target of 10 GHz. It is independent of the active transistor parameters.

peak_impedance.description: The magnitude of the tank impedance at resonance, which determines the required negative resistance from the cross-coupled pair to sustain oscillation.

sky130_expected.calculation: Z_peak = R_eq. With R_gd_A_1 and RL_1 both set to 500 ohms in parallel, Z_peak = 250 ohms.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Typical tank impedance for on-chip oscillators to ensure reliable startup with reasonable power consumption.

quality_factor.description: The Q-factor of the resonator, calculated as f_res / bandwidth.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Typical Q-factor for on-chip LC tanks and transmission line resonators in standard CMOS processes.

step3_testbench.description: AC analysis to measure the resonant frequency, peak impedance, and quality factor of the standing-wave oscillator's equivalent tank circuit. Both injection nodes are excited in-phase to isolate the even-mode resonance.
